It started frosting up then warming 5 / 40 degrees. Ordered parts {prime member} the parts came quickly and were not very difficult to put in, I had a high heat gun, but a hairdryer will work but, it will take longer. Unplug the fridge empty the freezer side only. Defrost all the frosted ice, remove a few screws, put in the part, easy peasy.  It will take about 24 hours for the fridge to cool back to normal temps, so stay out of it, and lowering the temp will not speed it up, only overwhelm the system. After about 24 hours, the fridge stayed at set temps; it has been about 3 weeks now, and the temps are perfect using the recommended settings.

My fridge wires for my original thermostat are copper and the ones on the replacement appear to be aluminum. Joining copper and aluminum requires you to use very expensive COLAR wire nut connectors that cost more than buying a new thermostat with proper copper wire.

Have replaced defrost heater, thermostat, and thermistor (all come with this part) on my 2002 GE Arctica PSS27SGNABS two times over the years. This latest time though the defrost lamp would not shut off after I re-plugged refrigerator. Tested and swapped other parts (I bought two) but same issue.

If this happens to you, don't fret. You need to check out Youtube (Grace Appliance) for diagnosing defrost system malfunction. Doing so, my main control board on the back of the frig was burnt on the back side of the board under the relay switch that controls the defrost cycle. Ordered a $200 control board replacement from Amazon (55X10942) and will get it Saturday.

I can't give this any stars.
Immediately after installation and plug in, there was a very horrible smell starting that smelled like electrical overheating. We thought the smell would improve. However, it got worse and worse. During defrost, the smell was worse.
It barely made any ice at all, then it melted the ice all over the freezer, then that would refreeze. Had to throw away a very nice thermometer because of melted ice that went into the door bin, then turned to frozen ice again in a door bin where the thermometer was.
After about 5 or 6 days, at around 6:00PM, it got so horrific, we got out the fire extinguisher, just in case.
I have asthma, the toxic Gas was getting so bad, I was coughing and chocking
By 11:00PM, terrified of a house fire, we had to unplug it.
The next day, we had to go buy a new refrigerator.
It is my opinion, that this kit must have come from a used refrigerator that had broken down from overheating.
I'm very glad we didn't have a house fire. In the future, searching for parts for anything on Amazon, we will have to be more diligent to search for certified new parts from a known seller.
We could have died.

Unplug fridge first. Keep refrigerator door closed to help keep it cool while you do the freezer repair. I only changed out the defrost element in the freezer. All's working well so have the other two parts for when they need installed. Was simple to do after defrosting the coils with a hair blow dryer for 20 minutes or more. Panel was held in by 4 hex screws. 5/16"? Two Phillip's screws, one on each end hold the defrost element in place. A plug on each end of the defrost element.
Installed everything new and let it run. After a day I noticed the Refrigerator Defrost Heater was melting everything then freeze again.

My 15 year old freezer started freezing up this month and Youtube videos led me to the conclusion that it may be the defrost heater that went bad. When pricing out the parts through GE or appliance parts stores that sell OEM GE products, all of these parts would have come out to $100-125 USD. I purchased this kit for less than $20, had it all installed in about an hour and it fixed my problem. It has been a week and my fridge is not icing over so I assume the heater is working as it should. I'll update my post with any changes.
When I took out the old heater, the sides looked black and burnt, almost like a light bulb that went bad. My thermostat was also bloated and a quick search online shows that bloated thermostats are typically old and worn so the fact that this brought both parts (and the sensor) most likely saved the day. It definitely saved money. Time will tell how long these last. Definitely worth a try before spending hundreds or replacing the entire unit.

Got this with intent to change heater only which mine was for sure bad.  After changing, the freezer froze over again after a week so I went back and changed the thermostat since it tested bad.  Since I had the new temp sensor with this package I changed it also just because I was in there.  After that, the heater started coming on and not going off for a long time, melting everything.  Turned out the temp sensor with this package was bad.  Make sure to test the sensor before installing.  16.6K ohms when set in ice water for a few minutes.  Mine read 12k or sometimes no load.  Replaced it with a new one that I tested before installing and now fridge is like new again.
